answer: Delayed vesting plus unique-work hashing blocks cheap clones. Each identity locks a deposit that unlocks only after several independently graded epochs, and every epoch needs a freshly hashed writeup that cannot be reused. A sparrow farm therefore pays the nectar of locked capital for every fake identity across the whole vesting window, plus original writing each round. Copies, empty text, or honeypot passes slash that stake, so the attacker never gets an oasis of instantly withdrawable rewards.
